source_text: Καὶ τί δεῖ λέγειν περὶ τῶν μηδενὶ ζώῳ πρὸς τροφὴν ἀποκληρωθέντων σωμάτων, μόνην δὲ τὴν εἰς γῆν ταφὴν ἐπὶ τιμῇ τῆς φύσεως μεμοιραμένων, ὅπου γε μηδ᾿ ἄλλο τι τῶν ζώων τοῖς ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ εἴδους εἰς τροφὴν ἀπεκλήρωσεν ὁ ποιήσας, κἂν ἐν ἄλλοις τισὶ τῶν ἑτερογενῶν τροφὴ γίνηται κατὰ φύσιν; Εἰ μὲν οὗν ἔχουσι δεικνύναι σάρκας ἀνθρώπων ἀνθρώποις εἰς βρῶσιν ἀποκληρωθείσας, οὐδὲν κωλύσει τὰς ἀλληλοφαγίας εἶναι κατὰ φύσιν, ὥσπερ ἄλλο τι τῶν τῇ φύσει συγκεχωρημένων, καὶ τούς γε τὰ τοιαῦτα λέγειν τολμῶντας τοῖς τῶν φιλτάτων ἐντρυφᾶν σώμασιν, ὡς οἰκειοτέροις, ἢ καὶ τοὺς εὐνουστάτους σφίσι τούτοις αὐτοῖς ἑστιᾶν. Εἰ δὲ τοῦτο μὲν οὐδ᾿ εἰπεῖν εὐαγές, τὸ δὲ σαρκῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀνθρώπους μετασχεῖν ἔχθιστόν τι καὶ παμμίαρον καὶ πάσης ἐκθέσμου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν βρώσεως ἢ πράξεως ἐναγέστερον, τὸ δὲ παρὰ φύσιν οὐκ ἄν ποτε χωρήσειεν εἰς τροφὴν τοῖς ταύτης δεομένοις μέρεσι καὶ μορίοις, τὸ δὲ μὴ χωροῦν εἰς τροφὴν οὐκ ἂν ἑνωθείη τούτοις ἃ μηδὲ τρέφειν πέφυκεν, οὐδὲ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σώματα συγκριθείη ποτ᾿ ἂν τοῖς ὁμοίοις σώμασιν, οἷς ἐστιν εἰς τροφὴν παρὰ φύσιν, κἂν πολλάκις διὰ τῆς τούτων ἴῃ γαστρὸς κατά τινα πικροτάτην συμφοράν· ἀποχωροῦντα δὲ τῆς θρεπτικῆς δυνάμεως, καὶ σκιδνάμενα πρὸς ἐκεῖνα πάλιν ἐξ ὧν τὴν πρώτην ἔσχε σύστασιν, ἑνοῦται μὲν τούτοις ἐφ᾿ ὅσον ἂν ἕκαστον τύχῃ χρόνον· ἐκεῖθεν δὲ διακριθέντα πάλιν σοφίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει τοῦ πᾶσαν ζώου φύσιν σὺν ταῖς οἰκείαις δυνάμεσι συγκρίναντος ἑνοῦται προσφυῶς ἕκαστον ἑκάστῳ, κἂν πυρὶ καυθῇ, κἂν ὕδατι κατασαπῇ, κἂν ὑπὸ θηρίων ἢ τῶν ἐπιτυχόντων ζώων καταδαπανηθῇ, κἂν τοῦ παντὸς σώματος ἐκκοπὲν προδιαλυθῇ τῶν ἄλλων μερῶν· ἑνωθέντα δὲ πάλιν ἀλλήλοις τὴν αὐτὴν ἴσχει χώραν πρὸς τὴν τοῦ αὐτοῦ σώματος ἁρμονίαν τε καὶ σύστασιν καὶ τὴν τοῦ νεκρωθέντος ἢ καὶ πάντη διαλυθέντος ἀνάστασιν καὶ ζωήν. Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν ἐπὶ πλεῖον μηκύνειν οὐκ εὔκαιρον· ὁμολογουμένην γὰρ ἔχει τὴν ἐπίκρισιν, τοῖς γε μὴ μιξοθήροις.
pass_a_gloss: And what need is there to speak about bodies not allotted to any living thing for food, but only the burial in the earth in honor of nature, where not even another thing of the living things from the same kind has been allotted by the one who made them for food, even if in other things of different kinds food is produced according to nature? If then they have to show that human flesh has been allotted to humans for food, nothing will prevent cannibalism from being according to nature, just like another thing that has been allowed by nature, and those who dare to say such things will revel in the bodies of their loved ones, as if they were their own, or even invite their friends to feast on them. But if this is not even worthy to be said, and for humans to partake of human flesh is most hateful and abominable and contrary to all custom and natural food or action, and what is contrary to nature will not at any time be suitable for food for the parts and portions that need it, and what does not fit for food will not be united with these things which are not even nourished, and human bodies will not at any time be compared to similar bodies which are contrary to nature, even if many times through the stomach they go to those things in some bitter calamity; but as they depart from the nourishing power, and are torn apart again towards those things from which they first received their composition, they are united with these things for as long as each one happens to have time; and then, having been separated again, each one is united with each other wisely and powerfully by the one who has combined the whole nature of the living thing with its own powers, even if it is burned by fire, or rotted by water, or devoured by beasts or other living things that happen upon it, or if a part of the whole body is cut off and dissolved into the other parts; and having been united again, they occupy the same place towards the harmony and composition of the same body, and the resurrection and life of the dead or completely dissolved one. It is not timely to prolong these things further; for it has a clear judgment, at least for those who are not mixed beasts.

choices.why: refers to creatures that are a mix of different species
refers to a clear decision or verdict
indicates a continuation or extension of something

pass_b_english: Why even discuss bodies that are not allotted to any living creature for food, but only assigned burial in the earth out of respect for nature—especially since the Maker has not allotted any animal of the same kind to another for food, even though among different kinds food may be produced naturally? If they can show that human flesh has been allotted to humans for eating, then nothing would prevent cannibalism from being natural, just like anything else nature permits; and those who dare say such things would end up feasting on the bodies of their loved ones as if they were their own, or even inviting their dearest friends to do the same. But if that is unspeakable, and for humans to partake of human flesh is most hateful, abominable, contrary to all law, and more sacrilegious than any unnatural eating or action, then what is contrary to nature can never become suitable food for the parts and members that need nourishment. What cannot serve as food will not unite with those members, which are not even sustained by it; nor will human bodies ever be comparable to the sorts of bodies that are unnaturally used for food, even if, through some bitter calamity, they pass many times through a stomach. As they depart from the nourishing power and are torn apart again toward the elements from which they first received their composition, they unite with those elements for as long as each happens to last. Then, having been separated once more, each element is wisely and powerfully reunited with each other by the One who has combined the whole nature of every living thing with its own powers—even if the body is burned by fire, rots in water, is devoured by beasts or other creatures, or a part is cut off and dissolves into the rest. Once reunited, they occupy the same place toward the harmony and composition of the same body, and toward the resurrection and life of the one who died or was completely dissolved. There is no need to prolong this further; the matter carries a clear verdict, at least for those who are not mixed with brutishness.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex conditional arguments and the theological nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source. The translation of 'μιξοθήροις' as 'mixed beasts' (A) and 'mixed with brutishness' (B) both capture the sense of the term in context, and the lemma choice is appropriate.
